beats.en: When you were very small, your world might have been just your home. As you grew, it became bigger. This short anonymous poem is about a young bird who learns, step by step, that the world is much larger than it first

textbookBox.concept: Think about where you see birds and what they do. Would you like to fly like a bird, and why? Also think about what a baby bird imagines about its world. The poem answers that question.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Think about where you see birds and what they do. Would you like to fly like a bird, and why? Also think about what a baby bird imagines about its world. The poem answers that question.
beats.speakEn: Think about where you see birds and what they do. Would you like to fly like a bird, and why? Also think about what a baby bird imagines about its world. The poem answers that question.

beats.en: The young bird says it first lived in a little house, and lived there very well. It thought the world was small and round and made of pale blue shell. This is the egg, so the bird remembers its first home.
beats.speakEn: The young bird says it first lived in a little house, and lived there very well. It thought the world was small and round and made of pale blue shell. This is the egg, so the bird remembers its first home.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 english · What a Bird Thought · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Next the bird lived in a little nest and needed nothing more. It thought the world was made of straw because the nest was made of straw, and it nestled close to its mother.

beats.en: Next the bird lived in a little nest and needed nothing more. It thought the world was made of straw because the nest was made of straw, and it nestled close to its mother.
beats.speakEn: Next the bird lived in a little nest and needed nothing more. It thought the world was made of straw because the nest was made of straw, and it nestled close to its mother.

beats.en: One day the bird fluttered out of its nest to see what it could find. It said that the world was made of leaves, but then it admitted that it had been very blind.
beats.speakEn: One day the bird fluttered out of its nest to see what it could find. It said that the world was made of leaves, but then it admitted that it had been very blind.
